name: dev-memory-records-count-as-material
title: Exclude committed dev-memory records from material and story-files hashes so the DONE gate cannot invalidate its own evidence
description: The DONE gate requires a dev_memory_finish_decision (missing_dev_memory_finish_decision blocks story_advance DONE). Recording it, and any dev_memory_capture it cites, writes tracked files under .proof-or-stop/dev-memory (experience.jsonl and finish-decisions/<story>.json). isMaterialExcludedPath in core/evidence-freshness.ts excludes only the story directory and gitignored runtime artifacts, so those dev-memory files count as MATERIAL: committing them changes materialHash and storyFilesHash even though no product source changed. On story B-a745 that single commit (ddf9189cba) invalidated every reviewer pass Prompt Envelope, every mechanical verification receipt, the 3x2 cross-host quorum, the DONE-required evidence and the certification window, forcing a TEST->DEV->REVIEW->TEST bounce, four lane re-passes, three fresh host reviews, a quorum resubmission and a second DONE-required run to reach a DONE that the code had already earned. The gate therefore mandates an action that stales the evidence the same gate consumes. This story makes dev-memory records lifecycle metadata for hashing purposes (or moves them under the story/runtime exclusion), adds a regression fixture asserting that dev_memory_capture plus dev_memory_finish_decision leave materialHash and storyFilesHash unchanged, and documents the ordering in the DONE convergence guidance.
